controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 1,360 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of TOI-1685 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (JWST NIRSpec). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

controls.label: JWST
controls.qualification: Published fit · Luque et al. (2025) · a JWST NIRSpec G395H phase curve of 14-15 February 2024 (program GO-3263), white light of detector NRS2, 3.823-5.172 µm · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature across 3.8–5.2 µm of TOI-1685 b from Luque et al. (2025)'s published fit to a JWST NIRSpec G395H phase curve of 14-15 February 2024 (program GO-3263), white light of detector NRS2, 3.823-5.172 µm. Their Fourier series becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 6° east of noon. Longitudes where the fit gives no emission are left blank. The false color runs from 350 to 1,450 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of TOI-1685's planets in this map from above, to scale, with TOI-1685 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

TOI-1685 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (19, 59, 86) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 28900646, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 4-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
